source_text: δὲ αὖται), πρὸς τὸ εἰκοσάπηχύ[ν] που διατετάν[ν]υσται μέτρον. Διὰ τοῦτό φησι· Καὶ ἐπιδιπλώσεις τὴν δέῤῥιν τὴν ἕκτην κατὰ πρόσωπον τῆς σκηνῆς, ἵνα μὴ τὸ περιττῶς ἐκτεταμένον τῷ τῆς αὐλῆς κάλλει διαλυμαίνοιτο. Ἐν ταύτῃ δὴ οὖν τῇ μεταξὺ τῶν ἄλλων καὶ ὡς ἑνδεκάτῃ τὰ ἱερά τε καὶ θεῖα τετάχατο σκεύη, διαμορφοῦντα ποικίλως ἔν γε δὴ σφίσιν αὐτοῖς τὸν Ἐμμανουήλ· τάχα που τοῦ ἀριθμοῦ καὶ τόδε κατασημαίνοντος, ὡς ἐν τελευταίοις τοῦ αἰῶνος καιροῖς, καὶ ὡς ἐν ὥρᾳ τῇ ἑνδεκάτῃ τυχὸν ἀναφαίνεται Χριστὸς, καὶ ἡ Χριστὸν ἔχουσα σκηνὴ, τοῦτ' ἔστιν, ἡ Ἐκκλησία. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Οὐδὲν, ὡς ἔοικεν, ἀπεικὸς ἐννοεῖν εὖ ἔχειν καὶ τὸν ἐπὶ τῷδε λόγον. {ΚΥΡ.} Μετὰ δέ γε τοὺς ἐπὶ τῇ σκηνῇ λόγους τε καὶ τύπους, «Καὶ ποιήσεις, φησὶν, αὐλὴν τῇ σκηνῇ, εἰς τὸ κλίτος τὸ πρὸς λίβα, καὶ ἱστία τῆς αὐλῆς ἐκ βύσσου κεκλωσμένης· μῆκος ἑκατὸν πήχεων τῷ ἑνὶ κλίτει· καὶ οἱ στύλοι αὐτῶν εἴκοσι, καὶ αἱ βάσεις αὐτῶν εἴκοσι χαλκαῖ· καὶ οἱ κρίκοι αὐτῶν, καὶ αἱ ψαλίδες ἀργυραῖ. Οὕτως τῷ κλίτει τῷ πρὸς ἀπηλιώτην ἱστία ἑκατὸν πήχεων μῆκος· καὶ οἱ στύλοι αὐτῶν εἴκοσι, καὶ αἱ βάσεις αὐτῶν εἴκοσι χαλκαῖ· καὶ οἱ κρίκοι καὶ αἱ ψαλίδες τῶν στύλων, καὶ αἱ βάσεις αὐτῶν περιηργυρωμέναι ἀργυρίῳ. Τὸ δὲ εὖρος τῆς αὐλῆς τὸ κατὰ θάλασσαν, ἱστία πεντήκοντα πήχεων, στύλοι αὐτῶν δέκα, καὶ βάσεις αὐτῶν δέκα.» Ἄθρει δὴ οὖν, ὅτι στεναὶ μὲν αἱ πρῶται γεγόνασιν αὐλαὶ, καὶ εἰς τρίτην διήκουσαι δεκάδα πήχεων. Εὖρος μὲν γὰρ αὐταῖς τέσσαρες, μῆκος δὲ ὀκτὼ καὶ εἴκοσι· αἱ δὲ μετ' ἐκείνας, εὐρεῖαί τε οὕτω καὶ μακραί· ἑκατὸν γὰρ ἐφ' ἑκατὸν, καὶ πεντήκοντα ἐπὶ πεντήκοντα, τρέχουσαί τε ἡ μὲν εἰς ἠῶ, ἡ δὲ εἰς ἑσπέραν τε καὶ λίβα. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Εἶτα τί τὸ αἴνιγμα; {ΚΥΡ.} Οὐχὶ δὴ τοῦτό ἐστιν ἐναργῶς, τὸ πάλαι διεπηγγελμένον διὰ φωνῆς Ἡσαΐου πρὸς τὴν ἐν ἐσχάτοις καιροῖς ἀναδεδειγμένην Ἐκκλησίαν· «Πλάτυνον τὸν τόπον τῆς σκηνῆς σου, καὶ τὰς δέῤῥεις τῶν αὐλαιῶν σου. Πῆξον, μὴ φείσῃ ἔτι εἰς τὰ δεξιὰ, καὶ εἰς τὰ ἀριστερὰ ἐκπέτασον.» Στενουμένη γὰρ ἐν ἀρχαῖς ἡ Ἐκκλησία Χριστοῦ, λοιπὸν εἰς ἠῶ τε καὶ δύσιν, καὶ βοῤῥᾶν τε καὶ νότον ἐξευρύνεται, καὶ διὰ παντὸς ἥκει τόπου. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Ἀληθές. {ΚΥΡ.} Ἐπιτήρει δὲ ὅτι τοὺς μὲν ἄλλους ἅπαντας στύλους τῶν δέκα αὐλαιῶν, καὶ τῆς ἀνὰ μέσον, χρυσῷ μὲν ἔφη διαπάττεσθαι δεῖν, βάσεσί γε μὴν ἐπερηρεῖσθαι διπλαῖς, ἀργύρου πεποιημέναις. Καὶ τίς ὁ τοῦδε λόγος, εἴρηται, καθάπερ ἐγᾦμαι· τῶν δὲ μακρῶν καὶ πλατειῶν αὐλαιῶν τοὺς στύλους, ἑτέρῳ διαποικίλλει λόγῳ. Ἀργύρῳ μὲν ἐκ κεφαλῆς εἰς πόδας καταγλαΐζεσθαι δεῖν εὖ μάλα φησὶ, βάσεσι δὲ αὖ ἐπερηρεῖσθαι χαλκαῖς καὶ περιαργύροις. Τύπος
pass_a_gloss: [cont. from §26: the eleventh (covering), across the breadth of the five (four cubits each)] diatetanystai (diateinō, is stretched) to about the twenty-cubit metron. Therefore he says: epidiplōseis (epidiploō, fold double) the sixth derris (covering) at the front of the skēnē, so that what is perittōs ektetamenon (stretched in excess) not dialymainoito (spoil) the kallos of the aulē. In this one between the others, as eleventh, the sacred and divine skeuē (vessels) tetachato (were set), diamorphounta (giving shape to) Emmanuel poikilōs in themselves; perhaps the arithmos also katasēmainontos (signifying) that in the last kairoi of the aiōn, as at the eleventh hōra, anaphainetai (appears) Christ, and the skēnē that has Christ, that is, the Ekklēsia. PALL.: nothing apeikos (unlikely) to think the logos on this also eu echein (is sound). CYR.: after the logoi and typoi on the tabernacle: 'you shall make an aulē for the skēnē, on the klitos toward lips (southwest), histia (hangings) of twisted byssos, length 100 cubits for one side; styloi 20, baseis 20 bronze; krikoi and psalides (bands) silver. So for the side toward apēliōtēs (east) hangings 100 long; pillars 20, bases 20 bronze; rings, bands, bases periērgyrōmenai (silver-overlaid). Breadth of the court kata thalassan (seaward = west), hangings 50 cubits, pillars 10, bases 10.' Athrei (look): the first aulai [sc. curtains] were stenai (narrow), reaching into the third dekas of cubits (breadth 4, length 28); those after them eureiai and makrai, 100 on 100 and 50 on 50, one running to ēōs (east), the other to hespera and lips. PALL.: what then the ainigma? CYR.: is this not enargōs what was diepēngelmenon (promised) through Isaiah to the Church anadedeigmenē (shown forth) in the last times: 'platynon (widen) the place of your tent and the derreis of your aulaiai; pēxon (fix), mē pheisē (do not spare), further to right and left ekpetason (spread out).' For the Church of Christ stenoumenē (narrowed) at the start afterward exeurynetai (is broadened) to east, west, north, south, and reaches every topos. PALL.: true. CYR.: epitērei (observe): all the other pillars of the ten curtains and the middle one he said must be diapattesthai (sprinkled over) with gold, eperēreisthai (rest on) double bases of silver; its logos has been said; but the pillars of the long and broad curtains he diapoikillei (adorns) by another logos: kataglaizesthai (be made splendid) with silver from head to feet, and rest on bases bronze and periargyroi (silver-covered). A typos [cont. §28].
pass_a_gloss_with_greek: [cont. from §26: the eleventh (covering), across the breadth of the five (four cubits each)] διατετάνυσται (διατείνω, is stretched) to about the twenty-cubit μέτρον. Therefore he says: ἐπιδιπλώσεις (ἐπιδιπλόω, fold double) the sixth δέρρις (covering) at the front of the σκηνή, so that what is περιττῶς ἐκτεταμένον (stretched in excess) not διαλυμαίνοιτο (spoil) the κάλλος of the αὐλή. In this one between the others, as eleventh, the sacred and divine σκεύη (vessels) τετάχατο (were set), διαμορφοῦντα (giving shape to) Emmanuel ποικίλως in themselves; perhaps the ἀριθμός also κατασημαίνοντος (signifying) that in the last καιροί of the αἰών, as at the eleventh ὥρα, ἀναφαίνεται (appears) Christ, and the σκηνή that has Christ, that is, the Ἐκκλησία. PALL.: nothing ἀπεικός (unlikely) to think the λόγος on this also εὖ ἔχειν (is sound). CYR.: after the λόγοι and τύποι on the tabernacle: 'you shall make an αὐλή for the σκηνή, on the κλίτος toward λίψ (southwest), ἱστία (hangings) of twisted βύσσος, length 100 cubits for one side; στῦλοι 20, βάσεις 20 bronze; κρίκοι and ψαλίδες (bands) silver. So for the side toward ἀπηλιώτης (east) hangings 100 long; pillars 20, bases 20 bronze; rings, bands, bases περιηργυρωμέναι (silver-overlaid). Breadth of the court κατὰ θάλασσαν (seaward = west), hangings 50 cubits, pillars 10, bases 10.' Ἄθρει (look): the first αὐλαί [sc. curtains] were στεναί (narrow), reaching into the third δεκάς of cubits (breadth 4, length 28); those after them εὐρεῖαι and μακραί, 100 on 100 and 50 on 50, one running to ἠώς (east), the other to ἑσπέρα and λίψ. PALL.: what then the αἴνιγμα? CYR.: is this not ἐναργῶς what was διεπηγγελμένον (promised) through Isaiah to the Church ἀναδεδειγμένη (shown forth) in the last times: 'πλάτυνον (widen) the place of your tent and the δέρρεις of your αὐλαῖαι; πῆξον (fix), μὴ φείσῃ (do not spare), further to right and left ἐκπέτασον (spread out).' For the Church of Christ στενουμένη (narrowed) at the start afterward ἐξευρύνεται (is broadened) to east, west, north, south, and reaches every τόπος. PALL.: true. CYR.: ἐπιτήρει (observe): all the other pillars of the ten curtains and the middle one he said must be διαπάττεσθαι (sprinkled over) with gold, ἐπερηρεῖσθαι (rest on) double bases of silver; its λόγος has been said; but the pillars of the long and broad curtains he διαποικίλλει (adorns) by another λόγος: καταγλαΐζεσθαι (be made splendid) with silver from head to feet, and rest on bases bronze and περιάργυροι (silver-covered). A τύπος [cont. §28].
pass_b_english: Cyril: …is stretched to a measure of about twenty cubits. That is why he says, ‘And you shall fold over the sixth covering at the front of the tent’ (Exodus 26:9), so that the part stretched out too far would not spoil the beauty of the court. In this one, then, set between the others as an eleventh, the holy and divine vessels were placed, which in themselves portray Emmanuel in many different ways. And perhaps the number also points to this: that in the last times of the age, at the eleventh hour, as it were (Matthew 20:6), Christ appears, and so does the tent that holds Christ, that is, the Church.
Palladius: There seems to be nothing unlikely in thinking that your account of this point is sound as well.

Cyril: After the words and types concerning the tent, he says: ‘And you shall make a court for the tent. On the side toward the southwest, hangings for the court of fine twisted linen, a hundred cubits long for the one side; and their pillars twenty, and their bases twenty, of bronze; and their rings and their bands of silver. So also on the side toward the east, hangings a hundred cubits long; and their pillars twenty, and their bases twenty, of bronze; and the rings and the bands of the pillars, and their bases, overlaid with silver. And the width of the court on the side toward the sea, hangings of fifty cubits; their pillars ten, and their bases ten’ (Exodus 27:9–12). Notice, then, that the first curtains were narrow, and their length ran to somewhere between twenty and thirty cubits, for they were four cubits wide and twenty-eight long. But those that came after them were broad and long indeed: a hundred cubits matched by a hundred, and fifty by fifty, one running toward the east, the other toward the west and the southwest.
Palladius: Then what does the riddle mean?

Cyril: Is it not plainly what was promised long ago through the voice of Isaiah to the Church revealed in the last times: ‘Enlarge the place of your tent and the coverings of your curtains. Fix them; do not hold back; spread out still further to the right and to the left’ (Isaiah 54:2–3)? For the Church of Christ, confined at the beginning, afterward widens to east and west, to north and south, and reaches every place.

Cyril: Notice too that all the other pillars, those of the ten curtains and of the one in the middle, he said must be overlaid with gold (Exodus 26:29) and set on double bases made of silver (Exodus 26:19). What this means has already been explained, I think. But the pillars of the long and broad curtains he adorns in a different way. He says they must be made richly splendid with silver from head to foot, and set in turn on bases of bronze overlaid with silver (Exodus 27:10–11, 17). This too would be a figure…

choices.why: δέρρις = 'covering' (the goat-hair covering of Exodus 26:7), αὐλαία = 'curtain', αὐλή = 'court', matching chunk 6.

LXX geography: πρὸς λίβα (Exodus 27:9) kept as 'southwest' (λίψ, the southwest wind; Hebrew has 'south'); πρὸς ἀπηλιώτην (27:11) = 'east' (Hebrew has 'north'); κατὰ θάλασσαν (27:12) = 'toward the sea', that is, west.

choices.term: στεναὶ μὲν αἱ πρῶται γεγόνασιν αὐλαί
choices.why: In 'στεναὶ μὲν αἱ πρῶται γεγόνασιν αὐλαί' the print has αὐλαί ('courts'), but the measures (4 by 28 cubits) are those of the tabernacle curtains (αὐλαῖαι, Exodus 26:2); rendered 'curtains'.

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of Cyril De adoratione Book 9 exists. Translated fresh from the PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the earlier English of this book was not used as a base.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; column may cut mid-sentence.

Boundary: §27 opens 'δὲ αὖται), πρὸς τὸ εἰκοσάπηχύ που διατετάνυσται μέτρον'; chunk 6 already rendered 'δὲ αὖται)' as '(and these are four cubits each),' at the end of §26, so §27 starts with the main verb to avoid doubling it. Bracketed editorial letters in the print ([ν] in εἰκοσάπηχυ[ν], διατετάν[ν]υσται) were read without the brackets. δέρρις = 'covering' (the goat-hair covering of Exodus 26:7), αὐλαία = 'curtain', αὐλή = 'court', matching chunk 6. Cyril's arithmetic (an eleventh covering 'across the width of five' giving about twenty cubits) is his own reconstruction and is translated as given, not corrected. LXX geography: πρὸς λίβα (Exodus 27:9) kept as 'southwest' (λίψ, the southwest wind; Hebrew has 'south'); πρὸς ἀπηλιώτην (27:11) = 'east' (Hebrew has 'north'); κατὰ θάλασσαν (27:12) = 'toward the sea', that is, west. In 'στεναὶ μὲν αἱ πρῶται γεγόνασιν αὐλαί' the print has αὐλαί ('courts'), but the measures (4 by 28 cubits) are those of the tabernacle curtains (αὐλαῖαι, Exodus 26:2); rendered 'curtains'. 'εἰς τρίτην δεκάδα πήχεων' (into the third ten of cubits) = their length falls between twenty and thirty (twenty-eight). 'ἑκατὸν ἐφ' ἑκατόν, καὶ πεντήκοντα ἐπὶ πεντήκοντα' rendered 'a hundred matched by a hundred, and fifty by fifty' (two long sides, two short sides). Isaiah 54:2–3 LXX: Cyril joins ἔτι to μὴ φείσῃ; in the LXX ἔτι begins verse 3, so the English keeps 'still further' with 'spread out', which fits both readings; his text also reads 'τὰς δέρρεις τῶν αὐλαιῶν σου' (the coverings of your curtains). 'Eleventh hour' cited to Matthew 20:6 (the parable of the labourers; also 20:9). The gold pillars on double silver bases refer back to §26 and Exodus 26:19, 29, where the LXX calls the tabernacle boards στῦλοι; the court pillars of silver on silver-covered bronze bases follow Cyril's text of Exodus 27:11 (περιηργυρωμέναι) and 27:17. The last sentence breaks off: 'Τύπος' ends §27; 'δ' ἂν εἴη καὶ τοῦδε Χριστός' opens §28. The English splits it as 'This too would be a figure | of Christ.'

changes: 'stretched out beyond the rest' -> 'stretched out too far' (περιττῶς)
Palladius' reply smoothed, negation kept ('nothing unlikely')
'reached no further than the third ten of cubits' (calque plus added limit) -> 'their length ran to somewhere between twenty and thirty cubits'
'both broad and long' -> 'broad and long indeed' (οὕτω); 'one side' -> 'one' (ἡ μέν refers to the hangings)
Isaiah 54:2 'Fix them firmly' -> 'Fix them' (no added adverb)
'on another principle' -> 'in a different way'; εὖ μάλα and αὖ restored ('richly', 'in turn')
